newsitem.title: USA: IBM ups dividend for 2nd time in a year.
newsitem.headline: IBM ups dividend for 2nd time in a year.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. said on Tuesday it will raise its dividend and begin a massive stock buyback to return cash to shareholders.

The dividend increase, IBM's second in less than a year, brings the company's quarterly payout to 40 cents a share, or 20 cents a share adjusting for a two-for-one stock split that was to be voted on Tuesday at the company's annual meeting.
IBM last raised its dividend in June 1996, when it lifted the payout level by 40 percent to a pre-split 35 cents a share.

The company said its board authorized an additional $3.5 billion in share repurchases, supplementing a budget that had dwindled to about $800 million after IBM's $2 billion in stock buybacks in the first quarter.
IBM's dividend is payable June 10 to shareholders of record on May 9.
Shares in IBM leapt after news of the moves, rising $4.375 to $154.75 in mid-morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
